Here is your annual management plan, saved to `farmer_plan_middle_male_12mu.json`.

---

I'm 58 this year, been farming these 12.4 mu since I took over from my father 30 years ago. I finished middle school, so I can read the extension leaflets and understand what the county technician says, but honestly I trust my own eyes and what Old Li across the ditch does more than any paper. My household has six people — my wife and I do most of the farm work, my younger son works in a factory in Shijiazhuang and sends money home, and my elder son helps when he's not doing construction jobs nearby. My daughter-in-law is here too, which is extra hands for cotton picking season.

I put 6 mu in cotton because that's my cash crop — the price has been steady around 7–8 yuan per jin and I know how to grow it. The other 4 mu I do wheat then summer maize for grain security and some income. I also keep 1.4 mu of peanut and 1 mu of mung bean — the peanut sells well at the market and the mung bean is for our own eating and some cash.

Right now the wheat is already in the ground and I topdressed it at jointing with urea; the extension guy said 15 kg per mu but I put about 12–13 kg because I also applied a bit more at planting last autumn and the plants looked dark enough. For cotton, I buy hybrid seed every year — saved seed weakens after one generation and then you get small bolls. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting and urea at flowering. Three irrigations for cotton — electricity for the well pump costs about 40–50 yuan each time for that area, but skipping irrigation in a dry July means losing bolls. I spray herbicide before planting and insecticide four or five times for bollworm; last year I saw aphids early so I'll watch for that. Picking is the big labor bottleneck — my wife, daughter-in-law and I do most of it but I hire women from the village for about 12 days at 90–100 yuan per day.

For maize, everything goes in fast after wheat harvest — sometimes the window is only two days if rain is coming. One application of fertilizer in the furrow, then irrigate twice. Peanuts get less nitrogen because they fix their own, but I give them phosphorus for pod development. Mung bean is easy — minimal inputs, one irrigation, harvest before August when the weather turns.

My total input cost this year is about **4,580 yuan**. That's a lot of money for me, but I've learned that trying to save 200 yuan on fertilizer and then getting 50 kg less yield per mu loses me 700–800 yuan. I'd rather sleep soundly knowing I did enough. I expect about 255 kg cotton lint per mu, 430 kg wheat, 470 kg maize, 290 kg peanut, and 110 kg mung bean if the weather is normal. I don't need to optimize everything — I just need to not have a bad year.
